what_happened: The command was STRAIGHT and then RIGHT, but after handoff the policy planned and drove a leftward lane change across the highway while the recorded path stayed in lane. It cut into the next lane to the left and sideswiped a car there (actor 41, the blurred car beside it in the camera), about 2.2 m off the recorded path.

On a straight multi-lane highway with the command STRAIGHT, the policy took over at 4.7s and started an unprompted lane change to the right. It cut into the adjacent right lane and its front hit vehicle 3, which was travelling alongside in that lane, at 6.4s.

The command was RIGHT and the route went ahead and to the right, but after handoff the policy planned and steered a sharp left across the multi-lane road. By 8.9 s it had crossed every lane at about 5 m/s and gone off the far edge, ending 13.4 m from the recorded path. No collision was recorded (collision_any is 0), so the failure was going offroad.

The ego was in the rightmost lane of a multi-lane road at about 6 m/s. The route (green) continued straight and later to the LEFT, but the policy's planned path (orange) bent right toward the shoulder. The ego drifted off the right edge of the lane onto the dirt verge and was off-road at 7.3 s, 3.6 m from the human trajectory. The camera view was clean before the drift and no actor was involved, so this was the policy's own steering mistake.

On the highway, the ego braked hard (21 → 8 m/s) and veered right, away from the recorded path and against the LEFT command, into the lane of the semi truck (actor 5) that was passing on its right. Its front hit the truck's side about 4.7 m off the recorded trajectory.

After the 4.7s handoff, the ego's planned path (orange) bent left, away from the route (green). The route continued along the highway and the command later changed to RIGHT, but the ego kept steering left across lanes at about 5 m/s. By 6.9s it had driven off the drivable area toward the concrete median barrier, 3.3 m from the recorded trajectory. The collision metrics stay at zero in all three frames, so leaving the road is the clear failure.

About 0.9 s after taking over in the rightmost lane, the policy planned a nearly straight path (orange) while the road bends gently left. The ego slowed from 18 to 15.6 m/s but drifted over the right edge line toward the curb and was flagged offroad at 5.5 s, only 0.7 m from the recorded human path, with no actors nearby.

On a multi-lane freeway with a RIGHT command, the policy planned a path that veered left, away from the route. The ego crossed the leftmost lane edge and ran off the road into the left guardrail/median at about 6 m/s, 7 m from the recorded trajectory. No other actor was involved.

With a LEFT command, the ego was in the right-side slip lane approaching the intersection. Its planned path cut left across the triangular channelizing island instead of following the lane, and it went off-road onto the island at 10.5 s while slowing to about 8 m/s; by then it was about 11 m from the human trajectory. The camera smearing appeared only after the ego had already drifted off the recording, and the logged rear contact did not cause this.

After handoff the ego started an unprompted lane change to the right on a multi-lane highway (route command STRAIGHT, then LEFT) and cut into the adjacent lane where vehicle 3 was traveling alongside. Its front-right corner hit vehicle 3, while the lead vehicle in its own lane was still about 12 m ahead.

On a multi-lane highway with a STRAIGHT command, the policy took over at 4.7s and steered right toward the next lane, where vehicle 4 was ahead and vehicle 3 was alongside. The recorded human path stayed in the lane. At 6.4s the ego, angled right, drove its front into the side of vehicle 3 in the adjacent right lane.

The policy took over at 4.6s in the rightmost lane of a multi-lane arterial at about 18 m/s, with no lead vehicle. The road bends slightly left, but the policy's planned path (orange) kept going straight and drifted right. By 5.5s the ego's right side had crossed the right lane edge toward the curb and grass strip, and the run was flagged offroad. The ego was only 0.7 m off the recorded trajectory, so it was a small drift, but it was the policy's own steering.

The policy took over at 4.6s on a straight multi-lane road with no vehicle ahead, and its planned path (orange) bent right toward the curb. By 5.5s the ego had crossed the right white edge line and was flagged offroad, only 0.7 m from the recorded human path. The table shows no collision, so this was a road departure, not a crash.

The ego was in slow highway traffic at about 5 m/s. After handoff it steered left, away from the lanes ahead, even though the command had changed to RIGHT. It crossed the left lanes and drove over the median barrier toward the opposite carriageway, and went offroad at 7.0 s with no collision recorded.

Traffic ahead was slowing on a multi-lane road, and the ego was in the rightmost lane at about 6 m/s. Instead of following the route (STRAIGHT, then LEFT), the policy steered right across the lane edge onto the dirt shoulder and was off the road at 7.3s, 3.6 m from the recorded human path. No actor was involved, and the camera view looked clean before it left the lane.

On the highway the ego braked hard (20 → 7.7 m/s) and stayed in its lane, even though the command switched to LEFT and the human went left. Truck 5, replaying the log, overtook on the right and merged left into the ego's lane, so the ego's front hit the truck's side or rear, likely a log-replay artifact made possible by the ego leaving the recorded path.

On a multi-lane highway, the ego braked hard (21→8 m/s) and steered right toward the next lane, even though the route command was LEFT and the recorded path stayed to the left. A semi truck (actor 5) was passing in that right lane, and by 8.0s the ego's front ran into the truck's side, 4.7 m off the recorded path.

After handoff, the policy steered left out of its highway lane while the route command said RIGHT. It drove across the concrete median barrier toward the other carriageway at about 5 m/s, ending 3.4 m off the recorded path. The camera view was clean before the drift, and no other actor was involved.

The ego was in the rightmost freeway lane at about 6 m/s behind slow traffic. After handoff its planned path (orange) kept bending right, away from the route line, which pointed straight and then left. It drove onto the right shoulder and off the drivable area by 7.2 s, 3.5 m from the human's path. The camera view was clean at 5.2 s, before the drift started, so rendering doesn't explain the mistake.

After taking over at 4.7s, the ego was driving about 6 m/s in the rightmost lane of a multi-lane road. Its planned path bent right toward the road edge, while the recorded route continued straight and the command later changed to LEFT. By 7.3s the ego had drifted about 3.7 m off the recorded trajectory, past the right road boundary and onto the dirt shoulder. The camera view was clean before the drift, so the policy steered off the road on its own.

With a LEFT command, the ego went into the intersection at about 10 m/s while the signal was red. It drove too far straight before starting a late, shallow left, then cut the corner and clipped the edge of the channelizing island at 10.7 s, about 14 m from where the human drove. The camera view is smeared because the ego is far off the recorded path, but the drift happened before that and it doesn't explain the late turn.

The command was LEFT, but the ego ignored the left-turn route and drove straight into the intersection against a red light. It then veered right toward the northeast fork and cut across the edge of the triangular island, going offroad at 10.6s about 12.5 m from the human trajectory. The camera was clean at 8.6s, when the ego was already heading the wrong way, so the later smearing came from the ego's own deviation and didn't cause it.

Right after handoff, the policy's planned path pulled right of the route instead of following the road's left curve. The ego crossed the right edge line onto the shoulder at about 16 m/s, 2.5 m from where the human drove.

On a multi-lane highway, the route command changed from STRAIGHT to LEFT and the planned path moved toward the left lanes. The ego slowed from 27.6 to 18.8 m/s, but instead of following the route left it kept going straight and drifted right across the right lane boundary onto the shoulder, about 7.7 m from the recorded human path. No actor was nearby, and the camera view looked clean until the ego was already on the shoulder.

The route command was STRAIGHT and then RIGHT, and the recorded path stays right. After handoff, the ego instead steered left across the lanes of a multi-lane freeway, heading toward the left edge. By 7.1 s it was 5.9 m off the recorded path and side-swiped actor 28, which was in the lane to its left (a lateral collision).

In slow, queued city traffic, the ego was following vehicle 24 in its lane. It slowed from 2.0 to 0.4 m/s but never fully stopped. It crept forward, drifting about 3 m left of the human path, until its front clipped the rear of 24.

The route command was RIGHT and the recorded path went right, but after handoff the policy steered left across the leftmost lane and the shoulder line. It ran off the drivable area into the median guardrail at about 6 m/s, 6.9 m from the recorded path. The camera view was clean before the failure, and the collision metrics stay at 0 while offroad is 1, so this was a lane-keeping or steering error by the policy.
